study.title: Purepu supraglacial-lake drainage, Rasuwa (8 July 2025)
study.question: Are usable Sentinel-2 observations available before and after 8 July 2025 over the Purepu lake source area, and what does cloud cover permit?
limitations: Monsoon cloud; terrain shadow; approximate AOI centre.
No volume or dam-failure inference from area alone.

aoi.boundary_source: Placed from published NDRRMA situation-report context; centre is approximate and has not been snapped to a verified lake shoreline.

can_conclude: Which optical observations exist before and after the 8 July 2025 event, at what validity, and where the observation gaps are.
Candidate snow/ice and surface-water index changes between April 2025 (before the monsoon) and October 2025 (after the monsoon) under an explicit seasonal caveat.
cannot_conclude: Discharged water volume, flood depth or discharge: lake surface area is not discharged-water volume.
The causal mechanism, or any casualty/damage claim from satellite differencing.
A clean immediate before/after pair: the only usable post-event July observation is the same-day pass at 63.2% validity.
interpretation.note: Feasibility verdict PARTIAL (docs/M4_FEASIBILITY.md): presented as evidence under constraint.

attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2020-2026), processed by ESA; L2A products distributed by the Element 84 Earth Search STAC catalogue (AWS Open Data). DEM: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA/DLR) where included. Event context: NDRRMA (2025) and ICIMOD (2026) situation reporting, cited as external literature, not project measurements.

limitations: Monsoon cloud; terrain shadow; approximate AOI centre.
No volume or dam-failure inference from area alone.
The following indices use 20 m SWIR bands resampled to the 10 m analysis grid and contain no genuine 10 m SWIR detail: ndsi.
Composites are robust within-period summaries of a few observations, not a dense time series; inter-annual change is represented by two period composites only.
Index differences are candidate spectral signals. They are not verified deforestation, wetland loss, construction, glacier damage or any other causal land-cover label.
Cloud, shadow and saturated-pixel exclusion relies on the provider SCL product; terrain shadow is not independently re-derived.
Surface reflectance is the provider L2A product; no independent atmospheric correction is performed.
Areas are planimetric on the documented projected grid; UTM scale distortion at this AOI is small but nonzero.

method.source: frozen M1 difference rasters + common-valid masks
method.threshold_rule: recorded primary threshold of each index (|Δ| ≥ t)
method.geometry: rasterio.features.shapes on the native UTM grid, projected to WGS84 (pyproj); no hand-drawn geometry
method.area_convention: pixel count × pixel area on the projected analysis grid

interpretation.title: ▲ Candidate NDWI increase · Region 01
interpretation.observed_measurement: Mean ΔNDWI +0.218 index units (median +0.204 index units) at the recorded threshold |Δ| ≥ 0.15; 7,481 px = 74.81 ha = 6.56 % of the 114,067-px shared-valid footprint.
interpretation.meaning: A NDWI increase here marks where the later composite reads higher in NDWI. This investigation is PARTIAL: no clean immediate post-event observation exists, and the processed pair is seasonal (April → October), so snow, ice and seasonal spectral evolution dominate the comparison.
explanations: Seasonal snow and ice evolution between the two acquisition windows.
Cloud, shadow and topographic effects at the mask boundary.
Event-related surface change — cannot be established from this seasonal pair.
interpretation.evidence_strength: Shared-valid coverage for this comparison is 100.00 % of the AOI (114,067 px). The region is a connected 7,481-px component at a stated threshold — adjacent pixels are not independent observations, so no significance is claimed. PARTIAL evidence study: the comparison is seasonal and explicitly caveated.
cannot_conclude: Discharged volume, flood depth, or confirmed event damage from these optical differences.
Any attribution of the mapped difference to the event itself.

input_measurements.index_label: observed index difference (later - earlier); not a land-cover verdict
input_measurements.band_resolution_note: computed on a 10 m grid from 20 m native bands; upsampled data contain no genuine 10 m detail
input_measurements.delta_definition: I_later(p) - I_earlier(p) on the shared analysis grid
input_measurements.threshold_rule: |ΔI| ≥ t, inclusive; sign selects the candidate direction

spatial_measurements.area_units: ha (projected analysis grid, pixel count × pixel area)

masking_and_cloud_limitations: Monsoon cloud; terrain shadow; approximate AOI centre.
No volume or dam-failure inference from area alone.
The following indices use 20 m SWIR bands resampled to the 10 m analysis grid and contain no genuine 10 m SWIR detail: ndsi.
Composites are robust within-period summaries of a few observations, not a dense time series; inter-annual change is represented by two period composites only.
Index differences are candidate spectral signals. They are not verified deforestation, wetland loss, construction, glacier damage or any other causal land-cover label.
Cloud, shadow and saturated-pixel exclusion relies on the provider SCL product; terrain shadow is not independently re-derived.
Surface reflectance is the provider L2A product; no independent atmospheric correction is performed.
Areas are planimetric on the documented projected grid; UTM scale distortion at this AOI is small but nonzero.
confounding_factors: Seasonal snow and ice evolution between the two acquisition windows.
Cloud, shadow and topographic effects at the mask boundary.
Event-related surface change — cannot be established from this seasonal pair.

method_provenance.algorithm: threshold candidate mask → 4-connected components (scipy.ndimage.label) → MMU filter → top-K selection
